a:r.a:t: Adenylate cyclase is now always (constitutively) active and produces too much cAMP from ATP.
Cholera toxin and pertussis toxin function this way.

p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing how the pathology of cholera results from defective regulation of adenylyl cyclase and overproduction of cAMP. There are three rows in this diagram. In the top row, a green snail-like structure with two projections at the top, is labeled “Normal Gs: GTPase activity terminates the signal from receptor to adenylyl cyclase.” This green structure has the following symbols on it, from left to right: gamma on the tail, beta on the first ovular structure, Gs on the top right, and alpha below it. The green structure is connected to Arg-NH2, [plus] NAD+, which is a NH2 bonded left to C, which double bonds up to O and left and bottom to a hexagon with alternating double bonds. The bottom of the hexagon is labled N+ and bonds down to H on a pentagon with three thick shaded lines around the base. Atop the pentagon to the right of the H is O. Moving left, the next point on the pentagon bonds down to H and up to CH2. To the bottom left, the point bonds up to H on the inside and down to OH. The configuration on the point to the left is the same as this. The CH2 that was described earlier bonds right to O, which bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O and down to O-, and right to O. This O bonds right to P, which double bonds up to O, down to O-, and right to O. This O bonds right to Rib in a rectangle, which bonds right to Adenine, in a longer rectangle. Below this, an arrow pointing downward, has a smaller arrow coming out of it to the right. It shows a hexagon with bonded structures leaving the reaction. The hexagon has alternating double bonds and an N at the bottom point, which bonds to C at the double bond on the right. The C doble bonds up to O and bonds right to NH2. To the left of the arrow is "cholera toxin" written in blue text. The long arrow points to the third row, which shows the previous green structure from the first row, this time, connected to Arg and NH2, which bonds down to the previous NAD+ structure, except the cholera toxin (described previously) is no longer attached. This new structure is labeled ADP-ribose. The green structure is labeled, “ADP-ribosylated Gs: GTPase activity is inactivated; Gs constantly activates adenylyl cyclase.”
